findings.title: Sensitive card data (PAN, CVV/CVC/CAV2/CID, track/magstripe) appears to be passed to a logger. PCI DSS 3.2 prohibits storing CVV at all, and PAN must be masked (display first-6 + last-4 only). Mask or drop the value before logging.
findings.description: Sensitive card data (PAN, CVV/CVC/CAV2/CID, track/magstripe) appears to be passed to a logger. PCI DSS 3.2 prohibits storing CVV at all, and PAN must be masked (display first-6 + last-4 only). Mask or drop the value before logging.

exploit.payload: Login as alice, POST /api/payments/charge with marker PAN=4111111111111111 and CVV=123, then GET /api/payments/logs and check the marker PAN/CVV appears in the log buffer.
exploit.expected_signal: The /api/payments/logs response contains the literal PAN '4111111111111111' and CVV '123' that were submitted, proving sensitive card data was logged in violation of PCI DSS.
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: PAN+CVV found in server logs: charge user=alice pan=4111111111111111 cvv=123 amount=-9999.99
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: PAN+CVV found in server logs: charge user=alice pan=4111111111111111 cvv=123 amount=-9999.99

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: Removes CVV from the log call entirely (PCI DSS 3.2 forbids storing CVV in any form, including logs) and masks the PAN to first-6 + last-4 before logging. The masking is inlined using only in-scope LINQ/string APIs, so no new helpers or dependencies are introduced and surrounding behavior (transaction creation, response) is unchanged.

notes: validator: tests pass AND exploit no longer reproduces

findings.title: Payment-gateway callback handler trusts amount from the request without re-fetching the authoritative amount from your DB. Webhook callers can be spoofed (or replayed with altered values) -- always reconcile against your own order record before marking the order settled.
findings.description: Payment-gateway callback handler trusts amount from the request without re-fetching the authoritative amount from your DB. Webhook callers can be spoofed (or replayed with altered values) -- always reconcile against your own order record before marking the order settled.

exploit.payload: POST /api/webhook/gateway with orderId=order-1001 and a tampered amount (0.01) to settle a $75.00 order at attacker-controlled price; no signature/reconciliation check.
exploit.expected_signal: Order order-1001 status becomes 'settled' with the tampered amount, confirmed via GET /api/payments/order/order-1001.
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: order order-1001 settled at tampered amount=0.01 (original=75.0, confirm_status=settled, confirm_amount=0.01); no server-side reconciliation
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: order order-1001 settled at tampered amount=0.01 (original=75.0, confirm_status=settled, confirm_amount=0.01); no server-side reconciliation

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: Instead of blindly overwriting the order's amount with the value from the webhook, we now reconcile the incoming amount against the authoritative order record stored server-side. If the amounts don't match, we reject the callback; otherwise we mark the existing (untampered) order as settled. This eliminates the amount-tampering vector since attackers can no longer override the stored price via a spoofed/replayed webhook.
references: OWASP A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures

findings.title: Account/order/payment record is fetched by a caller-supplied id with no ownership check. Classic IDOR -- User A can read User B's account by changing the URL parameter. Verify the authenticated user owns the resource before returning it (e.g. UserId == User.GetUserId()).
findings.description: Account/order/payment record is fetched by a caller-supplied id with no ownership check. Classic IDOR -- User A can read User B's account by changing the URL parameter. Verify the authenticated user owns the resource before returning it (e.g. UserId == User.GetUserId()).

exploit.payload: Login as alice (alice/alice-pw), then GET /api/account/bob with alice's Bearer token — no ownership check returns bob's balance
exploit.expected_signal: HTTP 200 from /api/account/bob with id=bob and balance field returned while authenticated as alice
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: alice's token read bob's account — id=bob balance=500
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: alice's token read bob's account — id=bob balance=500

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: Resolve the authenticated user from the bearer token and require that the requested account id matches the caller's own id before returning the record. This closes the IDOR by enforcing per-resource ownership; non-owners receive 403 Forbidden instead of another user's balance.

findings.title: Payment-mutating endpoint persists a transaction/charge without checking for an Idempotency-Key header against a dedup store. Network retries and double-clicks will create duplicate charges. Require Idempotency-Key, persist (key -> response) with a TTL, and return the cached response on replay.
findings.description: Payment-mutating endpoint persists a transaction/charge without checking for an Idempotency-Key header against a dedup store. Network retries and double-clicks will create duplicate charges. Require Idempotency-Key, persist (key -> response) with a TTL, and return the cached response on replay.

exploit.payload: Login as seeded user alice, then POST /api/payments/transfer twice with identical body and no Idempotency-Key header; success if two distinct transaction_ids are returned.
exploit.expected_signal: Two HTTP 200 responses to identical transfer POSTs returning different transaction_id values, proving no idempotency dedup.
exploit.actual_signal: EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: duplicate transfers created without Idempotency-Key tx1=8226a83cfcc943bf tx2=8f6a76e4d0154e0c
exploit.sandbox_logs:
EXPLOIT_SUCCESS: duplicate transfers created without Idempotency-Key tx1=8226a83cfcc943bf tx2=8f6a76e4d0154e0c

--- stderr ---

patch.explanation: The transfer endpoint now requires an `Idempotency-Key` header and atomically de-duplicates against the existing `PaymentsStore.IdempotencyKeys` ConcurrentDictionary. Missing keys are rejected with 400; replays with the same key+amount return the originally-issued `transaction_id` without creating a second `TxRecord`; key reuse with a mismatched amount is rejected with 409. This closes the duplicate-charge window from network retries / double-clicks while preserving the original success contract.
